newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan premier wants thorough probe of Yamaichi case.
newsitem.headline: Japan premier wants thorough probe of Yamaichi case.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto urged investigators on Wednesday to launch thorough investigations into the suspected involvement of another big brokerage in a widening racketeer payoff scandal.

On Wednesday morning, prosecutors raided the offices of Yamaichi Securities, which is suspected of giving about 80 million yen ($677,000) to Ryuichi Koike, the "sokaiya" racketeer at the heart of the scandal.
"I strongly urge (authorities) to investigate as deeply and thoroughly as they can," Jiji news agency quoted Hashimoto as telling reporters.
"Otherwise, public trust in financial markets will never be restored," he was quoted as saying.
Local media said Yamaichi, one of Japan's four biggest brokerages, allegedly made the payments in 1995 to obtain Koike's help in ensuring its annual shareholders' meeting went smoothly.
A government source close to the investigation told reporters on Wednesday that the firm had generally admitted to the allegations against it.
Payoffs to sokaiya, who extort money by threatening to disrupt shareholders meetings or by offering to prevent others from doing so, are illegal.
Yamaichi said in a statement it would cooperate with the investigation but declined to confirm or deny the allegations.

The raid by investigators from the Tokyo Prosecutors Office came just hours before the Finance Ministry was expected to announce stiff penalties against Nomura Securities Co Ltd and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) over the same payoff scandal.

More than a dozen people, including top executives from the DKB and Nomura, have been arrested in the affair, which coincides with the start of "Big Bang" reforms aimed at introducing more competition and global standards into Japan's long-sheltered financial sector. ($1=118 yen)
